findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_business, start_inbox, check_dns · Private data: get_business, report_door, ask_business, request_quote, request_booking, register_business, start_inbox, check_dns · Public sink: ask_business, request_quote, request_booking, start_inbox · Destructive: search_businesses, update_business, start_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_business, start_inbox, check_dns · Private data: get_business, report_door, ask_business, request_quote, request_booking, register_business, start_inbox, check_dns · Public sink: ask_business, request_quote, request_booking, start_inbox · Destructive: search_businesses, update_business, start_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_businesses" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
